narrative.summary: MERCOSUR's recorded AI text is a declaration of the ministers and high authorities on human rights of its States Parties, adopted in Brasilia on 24 November 2023. It sets seventeen human-rights principles for artificial intelligence, from human centrality, non-discrimination and data protection to transparency, explainability, human control and accountability. It is published by the MERCOSUR Institute of Public Policies on Human Rights and is not binding.

instruments.scope: MERCOSUR States Parties: human-rights principles for AI policy.
instruments.summary: Ministerial declaration of MERCOSUR States Parties setting seventeen human-rights principles for AI, including human centrality, equality and non-discrimination, privacy and data protection, universal internet access, information integrity, transparency, explainability and human control, accountability and complaint channels. It addresses algorithmic discrimination at work, gender and ethnic-racial bias, facial recognition, indigenous peoples' cultures and knowledge, digital education, social participation and multisector collaboration, and commits to active participation in international AI governance forums.

membership_note: The five States Parties of MERCOSUR: Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay. Bolivia became a full State Party in July 2024 and is still incorporating MERCOSUR rules; Venezuela is suspended, and Associated States are not included.
